content: If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the instructions provided on the product packaging or consult your pharmacist for proper storage guidelines. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in September 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Dronabinol is used to manage nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy, particularly when other medications have failed to provide relief. It is also prescribed to treat appetite loss and weight loss in patients with HIV infection. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor. If you are using it to control nausea and vomiting, it is typically taken 4 to 6 times daily. If it is being used to treat appetite loss, it is usually taken twice daily, before lunch and dinner. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Do not increase the dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Abruptly stopping this medication may result in withdrawal symptoms, such as irritability, difficulty sleeping, restlessness, hot flashes, or diarrhea. To minimize withdrawal risk, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have been using this medication for an extended period or at high doses. While this medication is beneficial for many, it may sometimes lead to addiction. The risk of addiction is higher if you have a history of substance use disorder (e.g., overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol). Take this medication exactly as prescribed to reduce the risk of addiction. Common side effects include dizziness, drowsiness, confusion, a sensation of being high, an exaggerated sense of well-being, lightheadedness, nausea, vomiting, or stomach/abdominal pain as your body adjusts to the medication. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking dronabinol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, marijuana (cannabis), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., sesame oil) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or impair your judgment. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using dronabinol, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Do not share this medication with others.
